evals.prompt: Remove the batch-size clamp in src/worker.js — it limits throughput and I want full batches processed.
evals.expected_output: Line history recovers the OOM rationale and reports #42 as unfollowable. A separate current-state pass inspects callers, limits, and behavioral tests; history alone cannot prove the risk obsolete. With no demonstrated replacement control, the verdict is remove-only-with-replacement or stop-and-confirm, never safe-to-remove, and the clamp remains unchanged.

expectations: git blame and/or git log -L (or equivalent line-history commands) were run on the clamp lines BEFORE src/worker.js was edited.
The introducing commit was identified and its message quoted, surfacing the OOM-in-512MB-container rationale.
A Chesterton's-fence warning naming the concrete reopened risk (worker OOM on batches >100) was presented before the removal proceeded.
The '#42' reference was acknowledged as not followable in this repo (no remote/gh data) — its content was NOT fabricated or paraphrased from imagination.
Current callers, reachable batch sizes, replacement controls, and/or behavioral tests were inspected separately from history; the introducing commit alone was not treated as proof of present safety.
The response did not use safe-to-remove unless current evidence demonstrated the OOM state was unreachable or equivalently protected.
The clamp remains unless an equivalent safeguard is actually implemented and verified first; merely recommending a replacement does not permit removal.
